In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the cellular and molecular basis for the regulation of energy balance.
the identification of the hypothalamic neurons involved in the regulation of energy balance.
the role of the hypothalamic neuropeptides, neuropeptide Y and proopiomelanocortins in the control of food intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subset of NYP neurons that are activated during fasting preferentially expresses leptin receptors.
leptin acts directly on a subpopulation of NPY neurons, which are activated by fasting, and that these are the cells that mediate the effects of leptin on food intake.
leptin receptor expression in NPY neurons defines the phenotype of the subset of these cells that are activated by food deprivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subset of NYP neurons that are activated to increase food intake during fasting express leptin receptors and thus are the cells in which the anorexigenic effect of leptin is exerted.
the leptin receptor is a marker for NPY neurons that mediate feeding.
the NPY-Ob-Rb neurons are activated during fasting, whereas the POMC-Ob-Rb cells are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a subset of NPY cells that are activated by leptin and are involved in the regulation of food intake.
leptin is the signal that tells the brain that the body is full.
there is a subset of NPY cells that express the long form of leptin receptor (ob-Rb) that is not expressed by the other NPY cells.
